unplanned_finding_SA4_SA5.title: spec_fallback never fires for the phrase 'wall hung basin' on THIS catalogue, in either SA-4 or SA-5
unplanned_finding_SA4_SA5.detail: Both SA-4 ('wall hung basin got SIRIM cert?') and SA-5 ('SRTWC286 and wall hung basin') show 'wall hung basin' resolving via the PRE-EXISTING trigram (match_tier:'trgm') code-text match, never spec_search. Root cause: the catalogue embeds descriptive words directly into product codes (e.g. 'MAB7029C-WALL HUNG', 'BRBC2296-1 (WALL HUNG)') -- the same cataloguing quirk the SA.md status banner already documents as the reason SA-P1/SA-P2's CRM gate fix was needed. Because trgm produces non-empty alternatives for 'wall hung basin' alone, the CRM's _result_has_zero_matches gate is never true for that token, so spec_fallback (the feature this whole family exists to test) is bypassed. SA-1 ('wall hung basin 600mm', with the dimension suffix) is the ONE case in this suite that actually exercises spec_fallback -- adding '600mm' apparently defeats the trgm collision. Both SA-4's and SA-5's hard/documented assertions still PASS (the per-candidate did-you-mean stays properly scoped, the known-gap description matches SA.md's own expectation), but neither case demonstrates the specific interaction it was designed to probe (F2's attachment-domain claim, SA-5's mixed-token claim) against the actual shapeA code path. RECOMMENDATION: a follow-up SA-4-variant using a descriptive phrase without an existing code-embedded substring (or the '+600mm'-style suffix that worked for SA-1) is needed before F2's attachment-domain interaction claim can be considered independently verified rather than inferred from SA-1 alone.

RED_first_gap.status: NOT CAPTURED as an independent n8n execution -- documented gap, not silently skipped.
RED_first_gap.detail: SA.md requires: 'run SA-1/SA-3/SA-4's inputs against the PRE-change clone rev [bd0023ac] first and record the executions... An SA-1 that was never seen red proves nothing.' Search of the manifest, diff doc, and tests/runs/ for a pre-existing bd0023ac-era execution matching any of SA-1/3/4's exact input text found NONE -- the only bd0023ac execution on record (12041903, referenced in tests/runs/access-tier-ask-rollup-20260811.json) is an unrelated access-tier-ask control turn ('promo for SRTBF11710'), not a spec-search phrase.
RED_first_gap.why_not_captured_here: Capturing a genuine RED baseline requires reverting the clone's resolve-entity-http jsonBody to the frozen before-body (tests/offline/spec-shapeA/resolve-entity.before.jsonBody.txt) via update_workflow+publish_workflow, running the 3 inputs, then restoring to be62b3a8 and re-verifying the sha. This is a WORKFLOW EDIT (write to the clone), which this tester's task explicitly prohibits ('Do not edit any workflow; do not promote') and which is outside the sorento-tester role's contract (never edits workflows). The manifest's own rollback recipe documents this exact toggle but frames it as coder/promote-adjacent tooling, not a tester action.
RED_first_gap.mitigating_evidence: The RED behaviour is not merely assumed -- it is provably deterministic by construction for SA-3 and structurally strong for SA-1: (a) SA-3's phrase ('purple levitating sink') cannot match any real product code or spec under EITHER jsonBody, because the CRM's non-fallback probes (exact/prefix/trgm) require some lexical overlap with real catalogue text that this fabricated phrase does not have -- zero-candidate is the only reachable outcome pre- or post-change, so SA-3's PASS does not depend on the RED baseline at all. (b) SA-1's phrase ('wall hung basin 600mm') is observed POST-change to resolve exclusively via match_tier:'spec_search' (5 rows, zero rows of any other tier) -- since spec_search rows can ONLY be produced by the new spec_fallback code path (verified in the CRM source per the diff doc §1, and structurally the feature did not exist pre-change / zero n8n callers pre-change per the plan §0), the PRE-change body is provably incapable of producing this resolution -- there is no other route to a spec_search-tier row in the pre-change graph. This is an argument from the mechanism, not an executed RED run, and is recorded as such -- it does NOT substitute for SA-P1's independently-completed CRM-side pre/post-deploy byte-parity check (already green per the SA.md status banner), but it does close most of the practical risk the RED-first rule exists to catch (a coincidental pre-existing route to the same answer).
RED_first_gap.recommendation: If an executed RED baseline is still wanted for the record, it should be captured by the coder or main-session (who hold write authorization on the clone) via the manifest's documented one-node revert-then-restore recipe, sha-gated both directions, BEFORE or immediately AFTER a tester pass -- not interleaved with a tester's read-only run.
